assets.pillar: The reformatting problem and how to fix it
assets.hook: Posting one video everywhere is not the same as posting well.
assets.caption:
Posting one video everywhere is not the same as posting well.

Each platform has its own shape. LinkedIn rewards context. Reels and Shorts reward a fast first line and a vertical frame.

I keep the idea and change three things: the first line, the frame and the ending.

It is slower than copy and paste. It also does not look copied.
assets.cta: Which of the three do you change first?

assets.hook: My first draft from an AI template ran long and cited numbers I could not source.
assets.caption:
My first draft from an AI template ran long and cited numbers I could not source.

I asked the LinkedIn Content template for a post under 150 words. The draft ran about 175, with figures that had no source, no hashtags and no call to action.

One rewrite by chat fixed the length, removed the claims and added a question.
assets.cta: Do you check every number in a draft before you post?

assets.hook: The first line decides whether anyone reads the second.
assets.caption:
The first line decides whether anyone reads the second.

I write the answer first and cut anything that sounds like a warm-up.

Weak: Today I want to share some thoughts on formatting.
Better: Black bars waste a vertical clip.

The second version tells you what you will learn before you decide to keep reading.
assets.cta: What is the first line of your next post?

assets.hook: I keep one routine for every idea: draft, edit, format, schedule.
assets.caption:
I keep one routine for every idea: draft, edit, format, schedule.

Posting stays steady when the routine is boring.

First I write the idea in one sentence. Then I get a draft, edit it by instruction, shape it for each platform and add a tracked link.

The edit step is where most of the quality comes from.
assets.cta: Which step in your routine takes the longest?

assets.hook: A clip finder found my moment but I would not post the file.
assets.caption:
A clip finder found my moment but I would not post the file.

I ran a 2:25 landscape video through Clips. It found one 32-second clip at 1080x1920.

Roughly 70% of the frame was black bars, I saw no captions in the frames I sampled, and the audio was quiet.

The finding step is useful. The finishing step is still on me.
assets.cta: What do you fix after a clip tool does its part?

assets.hook: Captions are the cheapest fix for a vertical video.
assets.caption:
Captions are the cheapest fix for a vertical video.

Some people watch muted, so a video without captions loses them in the first seconds.

Burn the captions into the frame, keep each line short, and read the whole video once with the sound off before you post.
assets.cta: Do you read your videos on mute before posting?

assets.hook: Editing a draft by chat is the part of IncuBrix I would use again.
assets.caption:
Editing a draft by chat is the part of IncuBrix I would use again.

I typed one idea, chose a single LinkedIn post, and got a full draft. Then I asked for three changes in one message: under 150 words, remove two unsourced claims, end with a question.

It followed all three.
assets.cta: What would you ask a rewrite to change?

assets.pillar: The reformatting problem and how to fix it
assets.hook: Resizing a video is not the same as reframing it.
assets.caption:
Resizing a video is not the same as reframing it.

A landscape video squeezed into a vertical frame leaves bars above and below. The viewer sees a small picture inside a big screen.

Reframing follows the speaker and fills the frame. It is one more step, and it is the step that makes a clip look made for the platform.
assets.cta: Do you reframe, or resize and hope?

assets.hook: Know what each step costs before you plan a month of posts.
assets.caption:
Know what each step costs before you plan a month of posts.

In my test, one draft plus one rewrite cost 17 credits, from 300 to 283. One clip cost 13 credits.

The balance stayed visible at the top, which made it easy to see.

Multiply that by your weekly plan before you commit.
assets.cta: Do you track the cost of each content step?

assets.hook: Turn one idea into three formats instead of three ideas.
assets.caption:
Turn one idea into three formats instead of three ideas.

I take one idea and write a LinkedIn post, a short carousel and a vertical video from it.

The first line changes each time. The point stays the same. That way each feed gets something made for it, and I only have to think once.
assets.cta: What is one idea you could reuse this week?
